label: prf:n-equals-1-vacuous-magic
title: Proof of n equals 1 vacuous magic
html:
Proof. Proof of n equals 1 vacuous magic

Proof

The claim reduces to a vacuous-truth statement about positive-integer decompositions.

  1. Suppose, for contradiction, that a decomposition 1 = n_1 + n_2 + \cdots + n_k exists with k \geq 2 and n_i \geq 1 for all i = 1, \ldots, k.
  2. Lower-bound the sum: 
      \sum_{i=1}^{k} n_i \;\geq\; \sum_{i=1}^{k} 1 \;=\; k \;\geq\; 2.
  3. By hypothesis \sum_{i=1}^{k} n_i = 1, so 1 \geq 2. Contradiction.
  4. Therefore no decomposition with k \geq 2 and all n_i \geq 1 summing to 1 exists.
  5. The universal-quantifier statement "\psi_1(q) \notin \overline{\mathrm{span}}\{\cdots\} for every such decomposition" ranges over the empty set of decompositions and is vacuously true.

Therefore 1 is algebraically prime at every q > 1. \square
